entries.appliesTo: any person making a campaign communication that includes synthetic media

dutySources.disclosure-ui: § 40 (ORS 260.268(2)) — 'A campaign communication that includes any form of synthetic media must include a disclosure stating that the image, audio recording or video recording has been manipulated.'

exposure.enforcer: secretary-of-state (injunction proceedings in circuit court; attorney-general for violations by or supporting the Secretary of State or a candidate for that office)

sources.disclosure: § 40 (ORS 260.268(2)) — 'A campaign communication that includes any form of synthetic media must include a disclosure stating that the image, audio recording or video recording has been manipulated.'
sources.scope: § 40 (ORS 260.268(1)(a)(A)–(B)) — '"Campaign communication" means a communication in support of or in opposition to a clearly identified candidate or measure, as defined in ORS 260.005' … 'a campaign communication may involve aggregate expenditures of any amount.'
sources.penaltyMax: § 40 (ORS 260.268(4)) — 'Upon proof of any violation of this section, the court shall impose a civil penalty of not more than $10,000.'
sources.enforcer: § 40 (ORS 260.268(3)) — 'The Secretary of State may institute proceedings to enjoin any violation of this section. The Attorney General may institute proceedings to enjoin any violation of this section by the Secretary of State, a candidate for the office of the Secretary of State, or any political committee or person supporting the Secretary of State or a candidate for the office of the Secretary of State.'

flags: Pre-existing regime reenacted: this act's amendments to ORS 260.268 are conforming cross-reference deletions only (bracketed removals of '[ (10)(c)]', '[ (10)(c)(B)(i)]' after ORS 260.005 renumbering); the synthetic-media disclosure duty, definitions, penalty, and exemptions are pre-existing law (chapter 9, Oregon Laws 2024) restated in the amendatory text.

Non-AI remainder: the bulk of the act is a campaign-finance overhaul — contribution limits (ORS 260.014), membership-organization aggregation (260.009), committee organization and types (260.042), unexpended-funds carry-forward (260.018), reporting and enforcement mechanics (260.041, 260.044, 260.083, 260.205, 260.232, 260.995), employee/contractor contribution coercion ban (260.416), and appropriations — fits no listed family, not coded.

Synthetic media defined as media 'intentionally manipulated with the use of artificial intelligence techniques or similar digital technology in a manner to create a realistic but false image, audio recording or video recording' (ORS 260.268(1)(b)) — reaches non-AI digital manipulation too.

Scope enum lossy: 'campaign communication' covers any communication supporting or opposing a clearly identified candidate or measure in any medium, and 'may involve aggregate expenditures of any amount' (ORS 260.268(1)(a)(B)); coded 'all-communications' as closest enum.

No windowDays coded: the cross-referenced definition in ORS 260.005 contains pre-election windows only in one alternative prong, and the other prong (express advocacy) has no time limit — no single window applies; per rule 4 only this text is coded.

Exclusive remedy: 'The remedy provided by this section is the exclusive remedy for a violation of this section.' (ORS 260.268(5)); court 'shall award the prevailing party reasonable attorney fees at trial and on appeal'; injunctions available 'without proof of injury or damage to any person' (ORS 260.268(3)).

Exemptions (ORS 260.268(6)): interactive computer services and information services under 47 U.S.C. 230(f)/153; bona fide newscasts with an authenticity acknowledgment; stations, websites, or platforms paid to broadcast/publish the communication; periodicals publishing with a statement that the synthetic media 'does not accurately represent a ballot issue or candidate'; and satire, parody, or content 'substantially dependent on the ability of an individual to physically or verbally impersonate a candidate without the use of technology'.
Operative date: 'The amendments to ORS 260.007, 260.041, 260.044, 260.083, 260.205 and 260.268 by sections 30, 31 and 37 to 40 of this 2026 Act become operative on January 1, 2027.' (§ 42(1)).
